studies.title: house studies
paragraphs: This study brings together a curated selection of residential buildings to explore how architectural composition shapes spatial organization and, ultimately, spatial experience. The houses included in this research come from a wide range of geographical and cultural contexts—spanning Europe, North America, Latin America and India. Despite these differences in climate, culture and time period, the projects share an important common thread: they are influential architectural works in which compositional strategies play a central role in shaping form, space and movement.

The selection of houses was guided primarily by the clarity with which each project reveals its compositional logic. In some cases, the organization of space emerges through geometric order and strong axial systems; in others, it is shaped by relationships with the landscape, spatial sequencing, structural expression, or the atmospheric use of light and colour. Rather than attempting to compile a comprehensive catalogue of houses, the intention was to assemble a focused set of examples where compositional principles are clearly legible and can be meaningfully compared. Projects that lacked sufficient documentation or where the compositional intent remained ambiguous were therefore excluded from the study.

This research approaches the houses through the lens of composition as an architectural language. Instead of analysing them only within stylistic or historical categories, the projects are understood as composed spatial systems—arrangements of volumes, planes, axes and hierarchies that structure spatial experience. Seen in this way, each house demonstrates how architectural composition functions as an ordering framework, guiding movement, shaping relationships between spaces, and influencing how form is perceived. Across different cultural contexts and architectural ideologies, domestic architecture repeatedly turns to a limited set of compositional strategies to organize space.

Methodologically, the study involves a process of reading, decoding and representing architectural compositions. Each house is examined through plans, sections and analytical diagrams in order to identify compositional elements such as axes, grids, hierarchies and spatial sequences. As part of this process, drawings with red and blue overlays are produced to decode compositional relationships. These diagrams make visible structural alignments, spatial hierarchies and circulation patterns, revealing the underlying order that governs each project.

Revisiting composition across such a broad historical range feels particularly relevant today, when architectural discourse often emphasizes technology, performance and digital form-making. By contrast, this study foregrounds the enduring importance of composition as one of architecture's most fundamental tools—through which space, form and experience are structured.

This publication represents the first volume of the research, documenting and analysing twenty houses that demonstrate diverse compositional approaches within domestic architecture. Conceived as an ongoing body of work, future volumes will expand the collection and continue to examine additional houses across different contexts and time periods.
